title: Agent-First Obsidian Knowledge Base
description: A public-friendly map of how the vault stores knowledge, routes writing, and uses agent skills without exposing private content.

principles.description: Agents start at indexes and descriptions, then drill into MOCs, notes, and artifacts only when justified.
Wikilinks are embedded in sentences so the surrounding words explain why a link matters.
Canvas, Bases, audio, dashboards, and reports orbit around markdown notes rather than replacing them.
The KB avoids vault-wide rewrites; skills repair one domain at a time to preserve context.
Plans, reports, trackers, and generated work live under ai-artifacts so the agent trail is inspectable.
This artifact explains the system shape, not sensitive personal domains or individual records.

props.title: The knowledge-base contract
props.deck: Every durable domain follows the same shape so humans and agents can navigate without reading everything.

props.content:
### _index.md

The entry point. It explains what the domain is for and routes readers into the right subtopic or note.

### mocs/*.md

Maps of content. They hold event, project, or topic clusters that would bloat the domain index.

### notes/*.md

Atomic facts. One concept per file, with a description field for scan-first agent traversal.

### artifacts/*

Raw evidence. PDFs, transcripts, exports, JSON sidecars, media, and source files linked from notes.

props.title: What belongs where
props.deck: The vault separates durable knowledge, active work, generated artifacts, and runtime configuration. That separation keeps the system sane.

props.caption: The same project can touch several zones: a newsletter may draw from the KB, draft in newsletter/, generate audio under ai-artifacts/, and publish via external tooling.

props.summary: Privacy boundary for this public artifact

props.content: This page explains the architecture, not the private contents. It intentionally avoids naming sensitive personal domains, individual records, private relationships, therapy details, or message threads. The examples are generic: job hunting, finance, content creation, fitness, housing, talks, and work notes.

A bare wikilink says only that two files are adjacent. A prose sentence says *why* the link matters. That lets an agent decide whether to follow it before spending context on a full note. The graph is navigable because the edges have meaning.

props.summary: How the writing system plugs in

props.content: The writing path starts with `writing-router`: load voice context, classify the job, then route to a narrow workflow such as newsletter outline, draft review, Bluesky thread, email draft, or cleanup. The rule is simple: one primary route, then a deslopify pass when the copy sounds too generic.
